Inspire, Believe, Achieve - Together
Welcome to Weston Turville CE School
At Weston Turville, we are committed to providing a nurturing, stimulating, and inclusive environment rooted in our Christian values. Our vision: "Inspire, Believe, Achieve – Together" guides everything we do, shaping our curriculum, our community, and our culture.
We believe every pupil is a unique individual, created with God-given value and dignity. This belief underpins our approach to education, where respect, honesty, perseverance, fairness, kindness, and trust are lived out daily. Our children are encouraged to be curious, confident, and resilient learners who embrace challenges with enthusiasm and a growth mindset.
Our curriculum is thoughtfully designed to inspire and engage, offering rich, exciting learning experiences that ignite curiosity and foster a lifelong love of learning. We work closely with families and the wider community to create a supportive partnership, enriching school life and ensuring every child can flourish both personally and academically.
We are proud to be at the heart of the Weston Turville community and warmly welcome you to explore our website and discover more about the vibrant life of our school. We look forward to welcoming you in person soon.
From the Headteacher, Ms Fitzpatrick, the staff, governors and families of Weston Turville CE School.

pageCache.pageTitle: Weston Turville Church of England School - SEND (Special Educational Needs and Disabilities) and Family Support Area
pageCache.text:
SEND (Special Educational Needs and Disabilities) and Family Support Area
Our SENCO is Mrs Gibbs. Her email is vgibbs@westonturville.bucks.sch.uk
Some children have special educational needs which affect their rates of progress and their access to the curriculum. Many pupils with special needs simply require their work to be adjusted in class so they can access it, while some require specialist assessment and adult support. Some children are supported through an EHCP (Education Healthcare Plan) which sets out what needs to be done to help them and how much adult support they should need. Others need a smaller amount of adult support. All of our children with special needs are given opportunities to be as independent as possible and are educated alongside the other children in their classes.
The school is fully accessible for wheelchairs and has disabled toilet facilities. There is a soundfield system in each classroom so the teacher's voice can be projected for those who are hard of hearing, and computer equipment is installed for those who are visually impaired. The curriculum is adapted for disabled pupils where necessary. For details please see the policy and local offer by clicking on the links to the right.

Early Years Foundation Stage
We aim to be a caring school that enables children to succeed as unique individuals and celebrates their achievements. We strive for a place where the children are inspired and develop interests in learning for life, within a happy, creative and secure environment. The Foundation Stage is the start of the children’s school life and we believe that we create strong foundations for the children which embed good attitudes for learning. These foundations are the building blocks to support children on their journey through a happy and successful life in education.
As a whole staff team we aim to:
Our intention is to develop an ethos in which all will thrive. Diversity and differences will be valued, respected and celebrated by all, and these aspects will contribute to the richness of our school life and learning.
The children learn within the prime areas of learning:
The specific areas of learning are:
Create self-motivating, self-disciplined, confident, independent thinkers
communication and language
physical development
personal, social and emotional development
literacy
mathematics
understanding the world
expressive arts and design

pageCache.pageTitle: Weston Turville Church of England School - Mrs Murty visits Weston Turville for World Book Day
pageCache.text:
Mrs Murty visits Weston Turville for World Book Day
We had a very special visitor on World Book Day this year. Mrs Akshata Murty, wife of the Prime Minister Rishi Sunak, visited our school, as part of her endeavour to see the very best of Buckinghamshire. Mrs Murty read one of her family favourites, The Gruffalo, to Class One in their natural habitat space outside. A grant secured through the Heart of Bucks supported the development of our Nature Reserve into an active outdoor learning space, and we were very proud to be able to show the results in such a special way. Mrs Murty is a natural storyteller and had the children - and adults - gripped!

Open Days for September 2027
Open Days for Reception 2027
If you are interested in a place in our Reception Class in September 2026, we will be offering prospective parents the opportunity to visit the school as follows:
Tuesday 13th October 9:30am
Tuesday 20th October 9:30am
Friday 6th November 9:30am
Tuesday 17th November 9:30am
Each tour will last approximately 30 minutes and will consist of a short presentation by the Headteacher/Class Teacher and a school tour.
If you have young children you are welcome to bring them along, but all pushchairs must be left by the entrance area. Should your child become unsettled during the visit we would ask that you leave the tour until they are able to continue.
